question.problem:
The matrix $A$ is given below. Let $\mathbf{a}_1$, $\mathbf{a}_2$, and $\mathbf{a}_3$ be the respective columns of $A.$ Determine if ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14144046/assets/b22e2ffa6f6d88665e120e8dad82961e72f8f4a99484e8f81de311a66ab25988.svg) is a basis of $\textrm{Col}(A).$ 
If that is the case, find $x_1 \cdot x_2$, where $\mathbf{a}_3=x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14144046/assets/28f79983a195fa0152832aebd334cd8e1aaaa977dd9016347a3152403fd390c7.svg)
question.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $A$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 9 \\ 3 & 1 & 17\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 9 \\ 0 & -5 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-\frac{1}{5}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So, a basis of $\textrm{Col}(A)$ is $\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2 \},$ that is to say,

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14144046/assets/4588c7d7ae4fd6cbc749373d83ab2d81e6a228f0cac03d5b959f4177f3f4cdf9.svg)

Now, since the $3$rd column of the reduced matrix is a non-pivot column, then the entries in that column tell us the coefficients needed to express $\mathbf{a}_3$ as a linear combination of all the other columns in the original matrix. So, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14144046/assets/fa2ad666a6b80eac26bad12db322fa361578d94327e230d7c520c950add78923.svg)

This gives us $x_1 \cdot x_2 = 5 \cdot 2=10.$
